'''Andrzej Mariusz Trautman''' ({{IPA|pol|ˈtrauman|lang}}; 4 January 1933 – 27 February 2026) was a Polish [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] who has made contributions to classical [[gravitation]] in general and to [[general relativity]] in particular.

Trautman made contributions to gravitation as early as 1958.<ref>Radiation and boundary conditions in the theory of gravitation, Bull. Acad. Pol. Sci., S´erie sci. math., astr. et phys. VI (1958), 407–412.</ref> The "Trautman-Bondi mass" is named after him.<ref>Chrusciel et al "The Trautman-Bondi mass
of hyperboloidal initial data sets" Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 8 (2004) 83–139</ref>

==Life and career==
Trautman was born in [[Warsaw]], [[Second Polish Republic|Poland]] on 4 January 1933, into an artistic family.<ref name="PAN_1">{{Cite web |title=Andrzej Trautman |url=https://pan.pl/czlonkowie/andrzej-trautman/ |url-status=live|access-date=4 March 2026|website=Polska Akademia Nauk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714171242/https://pan.pl/czlonkowie/andrzej-trautman/|archive-date=14 July 2025}}</ref> His father, Mieczysław, was a painter and taught drawing at a secondary school in [[Warsaw]]. His mother, Eliza Trautman (née André), was French, though she was born in Spain, where her father, [[Marius André]], was working as a French consular officer. His schooling, at the elementary level, was interrupted by the [[Warsaw Uprising]] of 1944. After spending about ten months in Germany, he returned, with his mother (his father had died in 1941) to Poland. In the fall of 1945, they both  went to Paris, to stay with their family there. In  France, Trautman attended a Polish secondary school from which he graduated in 1949 and returned to Poland shortly afterwards.

During the years 1949–55, he studied radio engineering at the [[Warsaw University of Technology]] where he earned his master's degree. Trautman continued the graduate work under the influence of [[Jerzy Plebański]],<ref name="FUW_1">{{cite web | author=Trautman, Andrzej| title=Short biography of Andrzej Mariusz Trautman | work=The Home Page of Andrzej Trautman | url=http://www.fuw.edu.pl/%7Eamt/cv4web.html | access-date=5 August 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127204656/https://www.fuw.edu.pl/%7Eamt/cv4web.html|archive-date=27 November 2024}}</ref> in [[Leopold Infeld]]'s group at the Institute of Theoretical Physics of the [[University of Warsaw]]. This Institute was to become his permanent place of study and work. In 1959, he obtained his PhD degree at the Institute of Physics of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] in Warsaw.<ref name="FUW_1"/> In 1961, Trautman and his colleague Róża Michalska spent a few months at [[Syracuse University]], at the invitation of [[Peter Bergmann|Peter G. Bergmann]]. The next year, Róża and Andrzej married in [[Kraków]].<ref name="FUW_CV">{{Cite web |title=Andrzej Trautman-CV |url=https://www.fuw.edu.pl/%7Eamt/amt-cv.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240727160831/https://www.fuw.edu.pl/%7Eamt/amt-cv.htm |archive-date=27 July 2024 |access-date=4 March 2026|website=The Home Page of Andrzej Trautman}}</ref>

Trautman and [[Ivor Robinson (physicist)|Ivor Robinson]] discovered a family of exact solutions of the [[Einstein field equations]], the Robinson–Trautman [[gravitational waves]].<ref>Ivor Robinson, Andrzej Trautman, "Spherical Gravitational Waves". {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130223182245/http://prl.aps.org/abstract/PRL/v4/i8/p431_1|title=''Phys. Rev. Lett.''  '''4''' pp.&nbsp;431–432 (1960)}}.</ref>

In 1977, Trautman identified the [[Dirac monopole]] with the [[Hopf fibration]].<ref>https://pubs.aip.org/physicstoday/article/68/6/11/415099/Historical-note-on-fiber-bundles</ref><ref name="JTP_16_561">{{Cite journal |last=Trautman |first=Andrzej |date= |year=1977 |title=Solutions of the Maxwell and Yang-Mills equations associated with hopf fibrings |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01811088 |journal=International Journal of Theoretical Physics |language=en |volume=16 |issue=8 |pages=561–565 |doi=10.1007/BF01811088 |issn=0020-7748|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1981, Trautman became a founding member of the [[World Cultural Council]].<ref name="WCC_1">{{cite web | title = About Us | publisher = [[World Cultural Council]] | url = https://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/about-the-world-cultural-council/ | access-date = 8 November 2016}}</ref>

Trautman died on 27 February 2026, at the age of 93.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wyborcza.pl |url=https://wyborcza.pl/7,75400,32632634,zmarl-andrzej-trautman-jeden-z-najwybitniejszych-polskich-fizykow.html |access-date=5 March 2026 |website=wyborcza.pl}}</ref>
